intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel — consider renting a budget compact car at the airport for the full trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north through the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Stop briefly at Akureyri if needed for groceries or fuel. Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10 and settle into your room. Take a short walk along the harbor to get oriented with the charming fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Take a gentle evening stroll along the waterfront and scan the sky for the northern lights — Siglufjörður's low light pollution makes it an excellent viewing spot. Bundle up warmly and watch from the harbor pier.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,000-1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or stop at a petrol station N1 or Orkan along Route 1 for a hot dog (pylsur) — Iceland's iconic budget meal at around 500-700 ISK
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cozy local café offering affordable soup and bread or fish dishes, budget around 2,500-3,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in northern Iceland — expect only about 4-5 hours of daylight. Road conditions can be challenging; check road.is before and during your drive. Dress in warm layers. Pick up groceries in Akureyri or Sauðárkrókur to save money on meals during your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður, one of Iceland's most award-winning museums. It tells the fascinating story of the town's herring fishing boom in the early 20th century. Entry is around 2,000 ISK — check if the hotel can provide a discount voucher.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the colorful streets and old wooden houses of Siglufjörður on foot. Walk up toward the ski slopes area for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding snow-capped mountains. The town is compact and very walkable. Visit the small local swimming pool (sundlaug) for a warm soak — entry is typically 1,000-1,200 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from the hillside above town or along the fjord road. Siglufjörður is surrounded by mountains that block artificial light, making it ideal for aurora viewing. Check the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast at en.vedur.is before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel using groceries purchased yesterday — oatmeal, bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka or a self-catered packed lunch from your grocery supplies
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available, or try the local grill/takeaway for budget fish and chips around 2,000-2,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — call ahead or check online. The local swimming pool is a great budget way to warm up and experience Icelandic culture. Wear microspikes or ice cleats on your shoes as pavements can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula on Route 76 toward Hofsós. The road offers dramatic views of fjords and mountains. Stop at any scenic pullouts for photography. Visit the Hofsós Swimming Pool, famously perched on a cliff overlooking the fjord — one of Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pools, entry around 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Stock up on groceries at the Krónan or Nettó supermarket to replenish supplies. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) for insight into local history and the famous Icelandic horse culture of the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via Route 75 and Route 76. Arrive back before dark if possible. Spend the evening watching for northern lights from the hotel or nearby hillside. Prepare a warm home-cooked meal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — bread, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Hofsós with fjord views, or grab a hot dog at a petrol station in Sauðárkrókur
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner using fresh groceries from Sauðárkrókur supermarket — pasta, local lamb, or fish

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Hofsós is about 60 km and takes roughly 1 hour in good conditions. Winter road conditions can be unpredictable — always check road.is. The Hofsós pool is outdoors and heated geothermally, so it is wonderful even in cold weather.

day_by_day.morning: Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Ólafsfjörður tunnel to reach Dalvík, a small fishing village on the Eyjafjörður. The tunnels are free and the drive is stunning. Walk along the Dalvík harbor and explore the small town. Visit the Hvoll Museum which includes a quirky exhibit on a giant man who lived in the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city, about 45 minutes from Dalvík. Walk the main shopping street Hafnarstræti, visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church (free entry), and explore the Akureyri Botanical Garden — the world's northernmost botanical garden, free to enter though most plants are dormant in January.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Akureyri's modest nightlife or dine out before returning to Siglufjörður. The drive back takes about 1.5 hours. Alternatively, spend extra time in Akureyri and return after dark, watching for northern lights along the fjord road.

meals.lunch: Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri offers traditional Icelandic lunch specials at reasonable prices — budget around 2,500-3,000 ISK, or grab a hot dog from the N1 station
meals.dinner: Akureyri has several budget-friendly options — try Strikið for a set menu or Greifinn for affordable pizza and pasta around 2,500-3,500 ISK before heading back

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a great place to stock up on any supplies you need. The Akureyri swimming pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) is excellent and affordable at around 1,000 ISK if you want a warm soak. Parking in Akureyri is free in most areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. If snow conditions allow, hike up the ski slope area behind town for panoramic views of the fjord. The Siglufjörður ski area (Skíðasvæðið) sometimes offers affordable day passes in winter — check locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum or revisit the Herring Era Museum if you want to explore exhibits you missed. Spend time in the hotel lounge reading or planning upcoming days. Walk along the fjord edge and look for seabirds and possibly seals near the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Drive a few kilometers out of town on Route 76 to escape any residual town lighting. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate, a blanket, and a tripod if you have a camera. The aurora forecast for northern Iceland in January is generally favorable on clear nights.

meals.lunch: Self-catered soup and bread at the hotel
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at Kaffi Rauðka or the hotel restaurant — budget around 3,000-4,000 ISK for a fish or lamb dish

day_by_day.notes: January in Siglufjörður can bring heavy snowfall and strong winds. Always check the weather forecast at en.vedur.is before outdoor activities. A rest day is important to recover from travel and cold weather fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður through the tunnels toward Ólafsfjörður and then continue on Route 82 along the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður. Stop at Grenivík, a small village with beautiful fjord views. Explore the shoreline and look for Arctic birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Laufás turf farmhouse museum near Grenivík — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farms. Entry is around 1,500 ISK. The farm dates to the 19th century and offers a fascinating glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. Return toward Akureyri and visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for a budget-friendly cultural afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Stop along the fjord road on the way back to watch for northern lights if the sky is clear. The road along Eyjafjörður offers unobstructed northern sky views.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Laufás or along the fjord — bring a thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel using groceries

day_by_day.notes: Laufás may have reduced winter hours — verify before visiting. The drive around Eyjafjörður is approximately 120 km round trip from Siglufjörður. Fuel up in Akureyri. The road conditions on Route 82 can be icy — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Mývatn, one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually stunning areas, approximately 100 km east of Akureyri on Route 1. Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. First stop: the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pots, steaming fumaroles, and sulfurous vents. Free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn area further. Visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations — a dramatic landscape of twisted lava pillars and arches, free to walk through. Drive around Lake Mývatn to see the pseudocraters at Skútustaðagígar (free). Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and cheaper at around 5,500 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via Akureyri. The drive back is about 2 hours. Stop along Route 1 near Akureyri for northern lights viewing if conditions are favorable.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Dimmuborgir or Mývatn lakeshore
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn for affordable Icelandic lamb soup before heading back, or self-catered dinner at hotel

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 200 km round trip from Siglufjörður. Start early to make the most of daylight. The Mývatn Nature Baths are a highlight and worth the splurge. Dress in very warm layers as the geothermal areas are exposed and windy. Check road conditions carefully on Route 1 in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a short walk around Siglufjörður harbor in the morning light. Visit the local bakery or café for a warm pastry and coffee as a treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upper valley above Siglufjörður on foot or by car. The valley road leads into dramatic mountain scenery. In winter, the snow-covered landscape is spectacular. Look for ptarmigan and other Arctic wildlife. Visit the small local church (Siglufjörðarkirkja) which dates to 1932.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights photography session. Set up near the harbor or drive to the valley road for a clear northern horizon. The combination of snow-covered mountains and aurora makes for stunning photography. Bring hand warmers and a hot drink.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to coffee and a pastry at a local café — budget around 1,000-1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Self-catered at hotel
meals.dinner: Self-catered — try cooking traditional skyr-marinated lamb or a simple fish stew with local ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Skyr is available at all Icelandic supermarkets and is an excellent budget-friendly high-protein food. January aurora activity in northern Iceland can be very strong — KP index forecasts are available at en.vedur.is. A rest day helps maintain energy for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along Route 76 toward Skagaströnd on the Skagi peninsula. The drive passes through remote and dramatic coastal scenery. Skagaströnd is a tiny fishing village with a quirky Museum of Prophecies (Spákonuhöfuð) dedicated to a 10th-century prophetess — entry is very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the tip of the Skagi peninsula if road conditions allow. The lighthouse at Skagaströnd offers views across Húnaflói bay. Return via Sauðárkrókur and stop at the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's finest historic turf farm complexes, entry around 1,500 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 200 km round trip. Stop for northern lights viewing along the dark coastal roads on the return journey.

meals.lunch: Hot dog or packed lunch in Skagaströnd
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel

day_by_day.notes: The Skagi peninsula roads can be very icy and remote in winter — check road.is carefully and ensure your rental car has winter tires (mandatory in Iceland from November to April). Glaumbær is a UNESCO-listed site and well worth the visit. Fuel up in Sauðárkrókur.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður valley, about 80 km from Siglufjörður. Visit the Víðimýrarkirkja turf church — one of Iceland's last remaining turf churches, beautifully preserved and free to view from outside (may be locked in winter). The surrounding valley is famous for Icelandic horse breeding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður valley. Stop at any Icelandic horse farms visible from the road — horses are often visible in the fields even in winter. Drive to the Kolugljúfur canyon near Víðidalur, a dramatic gorge with waterfalls that may be partially frozen in January — a spectacular sight. Free to visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy a warm dinner and spend the evening relaxing. Check aurora forecast for a potential late-night viewing session.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Kolugljúfur canyon
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður for a warm meal — budget around 2,500-3,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Kolugljúfur canyon is off Route 1 near Víðidalur — the access road may be snowy but is generally passable with a 4WD or winter-tire vehicle. The frozen waterfall scenery in January is extraordinary. Icelandic horses are friendly but always ask permission before approaching farm animals.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Tröllaskagi peninsula's eastern fjords. Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel to Ólafsfjörður and continue on Route 82 toward Fjallabyggð. Explore the small village of Ólafsfjörður and its harbor. The surrounding mountains are dramatic and snow-covered in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Siglufjörður via the scenic mountain road (Route 82) if conditions allow, or return through the tunnel. Stop at any viewpoints along the way. Visit the Siglufjörður swimming pool for a warm afternoon soak — a perfect way to warm up after outdoor exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Final major northern lights hunt. Drive to the valley above Siglufjörður or along the fjord road for optimal viewing. January nights are long (approximately 19 hours of darkness) giving maximum aurora viewing opportunity. Spend at least 2 hours outside if skies are clear.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch or hot dog in Ólafsfjörður
meals.dinner: Self-catered special dinner — splurge slightly on local lamb or fresh Arctic char from the supermarket

day_by_day.notes: The mountain road between Ólafsfjörður and Siglufjörður (old Route 82 over the mountain) is often closed in winter — check road.is. The tunnel route is always the safe alternative. The local swimming pool is an authentic Icelandic experience and costs only around 1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Siglufjörður. Take a slow morning walk through the town, revisiting favorite spots. Visit any local shops for souvenirs — look for locally made woolens, dried fish, or Icelandic candy as affordable gifts. The Herring Era Museum gift shop has reasonably priced items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive up the valley road above Siglufjörður one last time for panoramic views. If weather permits, attempt a short snowshoe or winter hike on the lower slopes. Return to town and pack your bags for departure the following day. Return any borrowed or rented equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Siglufjörður. Treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal at the best local restaurant within budget. Spend the evening watching for northern lights one final time from the harbor — a memorable send-off from this magical Arctic town.

meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch on the valley hike
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Kaffi Rauðka or the Hotel Siglunes restaurant — budget around 3,500-5,000 ISK for a special meal with local fish or lamb

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to consolidate any leftover groceries and avoid waste. Check out procedures with the hotel and confirm your departure time. Ensure your rental car is fueled up for the return journey to Keflavik. Download offline maps in case of poor connectivity on the drive south.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hotel Siglunes. Begin the long drive south to Keflavik International Airport — approximately 5-6 hours depending on road conditions. Depart by 07:00-08:00 to allow ample time. Drive south via Route 1 through Akureyri, then continue west and south toward Reykjavik and Keflavik.
day_by_day.afternoon: If your flight departs in the late afternoon or evening, consider a brief stop at the Deildartunguhver hot spring near Borgarnes — Europe's most powerful hot spring, free to view from the roadside. Alternatively, stop at the Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Húsafell if time allows — free to visit and spectacular even in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport with plenty of time before your departure. Return the rental car at the airport. Enjoy a final Icelandic hot dog at the airport or a coffee before your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast or grab coffee and a pastry in Siglufjörður before departure
meals.lunch: Petrol station stop along Route 1 — hot dog and coffee at N1 or Orkan, budget around 800-1,200 ISK
meals.dinner: Airport meal or packed snacks — budget around 2,000-3,000 ISK at the airport

day_by_day.notes: This is a critical travel day — check road.is the night before and morning of departure. Winter driving in Iceland can be unpredictable and roads may be closed due to snow or ice. Allow extra time and drive cautiously. Ensure the rental car is returned with a full tank to avoid expensive refueling charges. Keep your passport and travel documents easily accessible.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD essential for winter Iceland travel). Drive to Reykjavik (45 min) for a warm breakfast before beginning the long drive north to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the scenic drive north from Reykjavik toward Siglufjörður (~5 hours via Route 1 and Route 76). Stop at Borgarnes for a stretch and fuel. Continue through the Westfjords-adjacent highlands, passing dramatic winter landscapes. Arrive in Akureyri area mid-afternoon for a brief stop.
day_by_day.evening: Complete the final leg to Siglufjörður through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Check in to Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet welcome dinner at the hotel restaurant or nearby Hannes Boy restaurant, a beloved local spot serving fresh fish and Icelandic lamb. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Café at Keflavik Airport or grab pastries and coffee at a Reykjavik bakery such as Brauð & Co on the drive north (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Stop at Bjarteyjarsandur or a roadside petrol station café in Borgarnes for soup and sandwiches (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — fresh catch of the day or lamb soup (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions in January can be severe. Check road.is before and during the drive. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (Héðinsfjarðargöng) is the main access to Siglufjörður and may close in extreme weather. Keep emergency supplies in the car. Sunset is around 15:30 in January so most of the drive will be in darkness — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: After a good rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a morning walk around Siglufjörður town — one of Iceland's most charming fishing villages. Visit the iconic red harbour warehouses and the waterfront. Pop into the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) when it opens — a fascinating look at the town's herring boom history (~1,500 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the short scenic route around the Siglufjörður fjord. Explore the surrounding snow-covered mountains on a gentle winter hike near the town — the terrain around Siglufjörður offers beautiful low-level walks even in winter. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a warm geothermal soak — a true local experience (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and prepare for northern lights watching. Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it excellent for aurora viewing. Check aurora forecast on vedur.is (aim for KP index 3+). Bundle up and walk to the harbour or hillside above town for unobstructed sky views. If clouds permit, this could be your first aurora sighting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet (included or ~2,500 ISK) — expect skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka café in Siglufjörður — homemade soups, sandwiches, and excellent coffee (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — Icelandic lamb or Arctic char with seasonal vegetables (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in Siglufjörður — sunrise around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30. Plan outdoor activities around this narrow daylight window. The town is very quiet in winter which adds to its magical atmosphere. Dress in thermal layers at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along Route 76 to Ólafsfjörður (30 min) and then continue to Dalvík (another 30 min). From Dalvík, take the ferry to Hrísey island — known as the 'Pearl of Eyjafjörður.' The island is a peaceful nature reserve with abundant birdlife even in winter. Walk the marked trails and enjoy the serene Arctic atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by ferry to Dalvík and drive south to Akureyri (35 min), Iceland's second-largest city. Explore the charming town centre — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, browse the small shops on Hafnarstræti, and visit the Akureyri Art Museum if open.
day_by_day.evening: Soak at Akureyri's geothermal swimming pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a wonderful local hot pot experience with mountain views (~1,000 ISK). Drive back to Siglufjörður (1 hour). Keep eyes on the sky for northern lights on the return drive through dark fjord roads.

meals.lunch: Café in Dalvík or pack a lunch from the hotel — simple sandwiches and thermos of hot coffee for the ferry trip
meals.dinner: Rub23 restaurant in Akureyri before heading back — excellent sushi and Icelandic fusion, mid-range pricing (~5,500–7,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Check Hrísey ferry schedule in advance at hrisey.is — winter schedules are reduced. The drive between Siglufjörður and Akureyri is stunning but can be icy. Allow extra time and drive cautiously. Akureyri has good supermarkets (Krónan, Nettó) — stock up on snacks and supplies for the hotel room.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður toward the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Head to Hofsós (about 1.5 hours via Route 76 and Route 75) — a tiny village with one of Iceland's most dramatically situated swimming pools, the Hofsós Infinity Pool, perched above Skagafjörður with panoramic fjord views. Arrive early to enjoy it in relative solitude (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur (30 min from Hofsós), the largest town in Skagafjörður. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum for insight into the region's Viking and farming history. Walk along the harbour and explore the town. Drive back toward Siglufjörður via the scenic mountain road (if conditions allow) or the tunnel route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Spend the evening on a self-guided northern lights hunt — drive a few kilometres out of town toward Héðinsfjörður (before the tunnel) for a dark sky spot with mountain backdrop. Bring a tripod if you have a camera. Hot chocolate in a thermos is essential.

meals.lunch: Café Ólafs in Sauðárkrókur or local bakery — lamb soup and fresh bread (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel room with groceries from Sauðárkrókur supermarket, or Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður (~3,000–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is one of Iceland's hidden gems — far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon but equally spectacular. Bring your own towel or rent one on site. Check pool opening hours in advance as winter hours may be limited. The mountain road over Tröllaskagi (Route 748) is often closed in winter — always check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lake Mývatn area (about 2 hours east of Siglufjörður via Akureyri). Depart early. First stop: Goðafoss waterfall — the 'Waterfall of the Gods,' one of Iceland's most beautiful and accessible waterfalls, stunning in winter with ice formations along the banks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Mývatn Nature Baths — Iceland's northern answer to the Blue Lagoon, set in a dramatic volcanic landscape. Soak in the mineral-rich geothermal lagoon with views of the surrounding lava fields (~5,500 ISK). Afterward, drive around Lake Mývatn to see the Dimmuborgir lava formations and Hverfjall crater (exterior views in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Visit Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pots, steaming fumaroles, and sulfurous vents glowing eerily in the dark. Begin the drive back to Siglufjörður, arriving by 21:00–22:00. Watch for northern lights on the return journey through the dark highland roads.

meals.lunch: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn — traditional Icelandic lamb soup and rye bread baked in geothermal ground (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant at Mývatn (if timing works) — famous for geothermally baked rye bread and fresh dairy, or pack dinner to eat at hotel (~4,000–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly less crowded and more affordable than the Blue Lagoon, with a similarly magical atmosphere. Book in advance online. The drive from Siglufjörður to Mývatn is long — this is a full day trip. Fuel up in Akureyri on the way. Námaskarð is free and open 24 hours — spectacular at night.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning in Siglufjörður — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the town's small but excellent Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) which celebrates Iceland's musical heritage. Browse the local shops and pick up Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters) at the local craft store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing or winter hiking on the slopes above Siglufjörður — the town is surrounded by dramatic mountains that are popular ski terrain. Rent snowshoes locally or simply walk the lower marked paths. The views over the fjord from the hillsides are extraordinary. Return to town for a warm-up at the local pool.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — book a guided tour departing from Akureyri (1 hour drive) with a local operator such as Ambassador Travel or Arctic Adventures. Guides use real-time aurora forecasts and drive to optimal viewing locations away from any light pollution. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00 (~10,000–12,000 ISK).

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — leisurely breakfast with skyr, fresh bread, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — homemade cake and soup special (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Early dinner at Hotel Siglunes before the evening tour — fish of the day or lamb stew (~5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book the northern lights tour well in advance as winter tours fill up quickly. Most reputable operators offer a free repeat tour if aurora activity is too low on your booked night — confirm this policy when booking. Dress in your warmest layers for the tour; standing outside in January in Iceland is extremely cold.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 4–4.5 hours). This is a travel day with scenic stops. Pass through Akureyri and continue west along Route 1. Stop at Hvammstangi to visit the Icelandic Seal Centre and look for seals along the coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Arrive at Snæfellsjökull National Park. Drive the peninsula's southern coast, stopping at Búðakirkja — the iconic black church set against the glacier. Visit Arnarstapi village with its dramatic basalt sea cliffs and natural arches carved by the Atlantic.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a guesthouse or hotel in Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur for the night (pre-booked mid-range accommodation). Dinner in town. Watch for northern lights over the peninsula — Kirkjufell mountain near Grundarfjörður is one of Iceland's most photographed aurora backdrops.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes final breakfast before checkout
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Hvammstangi or Borgarnes — petrol station café or local bakery (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Grundarfjörður — excellent seafood with views of Kirkjufell (~5,500–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — start early. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' as it contains glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, and dramatic coastline all in one area. Kirkjufell mountain with its waterfall (Kirkjufellsfoss) is unmissable — especially magical if aurora appears overhead. Check road conditions carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Full day exploring Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Morning: Drive to Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach — a hauntingly beautiful cove with rusted shipwreck remains and dramatic sea stacks. Continue to Saxhóll crater for a short climb (if icy conditions allow) with panoramic views over the lava fields toward the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Snæfellsjökull glacier — the mystical glacier made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth.' Take a guided snowcat or snowmobile tour on the glacier with a local operator (Snjófell or similar, ~15,000–20,000 ISK). Alternatively, visit the glacier viewpoint and explore the lava tube cave at Vatnshellir (~2,500 ISK guided tour).
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Stykkishólmur — the charming main town of the peninsula. Explore the colourful harbour and the distinctive Library of Water art installation. Dinner in town. Aurora watch from the harbour or hillside above town — excellent dark sky location.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop at Hellissandur village near the glacier (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Narfeyrarstofa restaurant in Stykkishólmur — renowned for fresh seafood and local ingredients (~6,000–8,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Vatnshellir lava tube tour is highly recommended — a unique underground experience with dramatic geological formations. Book in advance. Glacier tours require good weather and visibility — have a backup plan. The peninsula's west end has very limited services in winter so carry extra fuel and food.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Snæfellsnes back toward Reykjavik (2 hours). Stop at the Settlement Centre in Borgarnes — an excellent museum covering Iceland's Viking settlement history and the Egils Saga (~2,500 ISK). Well worth 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik. Check in to a mid-range hotel in the city centre (pre-booked — options like Centerhotel Þingholt or Hotel Borg offer good value). Explore the city: walk Laugavegur shopping street, visit Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top for city views (~1,000 ISK), and stroll the old harbour area.
day_by_day.evening: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience — book the evening slot (17:00–21:00) for a magical experience in the milky-blue waters under the dark sky. The Blue Lagoon is 45 minutes from Reykjavik. Comfort package includes silica mud mask and one drink (~12,000–15,000 ISK). Book well in advance — this is essential.

meals.lunch: Settlement Centre café in Borgarnes — excellent lamb soup and homemade bread (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Light meal before Blue Lagoon (they have an in-water bar for drinks) — grab a bowl at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik for traditional Icelandic cuisine (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be booked online well in advance — it sells out weeks ahead, especially evening slots. The evening experience is particularly magical in winter with steam rising against the dark sky. Bring flip flops and a hair tie. Silica mud is provided. The lagoon is located near Keflavik airport — convenient for later in the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle day trip from Reykjavik. Depart early. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi) was founded. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley in the crisp winter air. Stunning in snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 metres into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall — the 'Golden Falls,' one of Iceland's most powerful and dramatic waterfalls, often partially frozen in January with spectacular ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik via the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool (built 1891), a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser. Far more authentic and affordable than the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK). Return to Reykjavik for dinner.

meals.lunch: Geysir Centre café — lamb soup and Icelandic meat soup (~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) in Reykjavik — Icelandic ingredients cooked over lava stone grill, mid-range splurge (~7,000–9,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is Iceland's most popular tourist route but remains spectacular in winter with far fewer crowds than summer. Dress very warmly at Gullfoss — the spray from the falls creates an icy mist. The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is a wonderful alternative to the Blue Lagoon — more rustic, more authentic, and significantly cheaper. Book online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park. Join a guided snorkel tour between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 metres. The water is 2–4°C but dry suits keep you warm. One of the world's top dive/snorkel sites (~25,000–30,000 ISK for snorkeling). Depart Reykjavik by 08:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik by early afternoon. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Hafnarhús) or the National Museum of Iceland for cultural enrichment (~2,000 ISK). Explore the Grandi harbour district — a hip area with street art, the Whales of Iceland exhibition, and excellent coffee shops.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour from Reykjavik — join a guided minibus tour with a local operator (Reykjavik Excursions, Arctic Adventures, or similar). Guides monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive to the best viewing spots outside the city. Tours run approximately 21:00–01:00 (~9,000–12,000 ISK). This is your best guided aurora opportunity near Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before Silfra departure
meals.lunch: Café in Þingvellir visitor centre or packed lunch (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbour — famous for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers, excellent value (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires advance booking — tours fill up fast. You must be a confident swimmer. The dry suit keeps you warm but your face will be cold — this is normal. The visibility in Silfra is extraordinary and the colours of the water are unlike anything else on Earth. Bring a waterproof camera or GoPro. Minimum age typically 12 years.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast day trip from Reykjavik. Drive east along Route 1. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — walk behind the curtain of water (may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic, with a staircase to the top offering views over the black sand coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), powerful Atlantic waves, and black volcanic sand. Exercise extreme caution — sneaker waves are deadly here. Visit the Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic coastal views (if accessible in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik, stopping at Seljavallalaug — one of Iceland's oldest swimming pools, a geothermal pool tucked into a mountain valley (free, bring your own towel, short hike required). Arrive back in Reykjavik for a final city dinner. Explore the lively Laugavegur bar and restaurant scene.

meals.lunch: Skál! café in Vík or the Black Beach Restaurant near Reynisfjara — lamb burger or fish and chips (~3,000–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro in Reykjavik — French-Icelandic bistro with excellent fish dishes and a warm atmosphere (~6,000–8,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: Reynisfjara black sand beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves that have killed tourists. Never turn your back on the ocean and stay well back from the waterline. Seljavallalaug pool requires a 15-minute walk along a river valley — can be muddy or icy in January. Bring a headlamp as it gets dark early. The South Coast is stunning even in winter — often snow-capped mountains meet black sand beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and a last walk through the city. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) on the waterfront — iconic Viking ship sculpture with views across the bay to Mount Esja. Browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or Laugavegur for last-minute souvenirs — Icelandic wool, lava salt, skyr, and local chocolate make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel and drive to Keflavik Airport (45 min). Allow extra time for winter road conditions and airport security. Return rental car. Enjoy a final Icelandic meal at the airport or nearby. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, hot springs, glaciers, waterfalls, and Arctic wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Carry memories of Iceland's otherworldly landscapes, the dancing aurora, the warmth of geothermal pools against the Arctic cold, and the unique magic of the world's northernmost capital.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final skyr and smoked salmon spread
meals.lunch: Kaffi Duus in Keflavik town (near airport) — excellent fish soup and harbour views (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavik — Icelandic lamb or fish (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank of fuel — petrol stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for car return, shuttle, and check-in. Duty-free at Keflavik is excellent — Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolate, and wool products at good prices. Iceland's 11% VAT can be reclaimed at the airport for purchases over 6,000 ISK — keep your receipts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then transfer via pre-arranged luxury private car service northward toward Siglufjörður. The scenic drive (~5 hours) winds through dramatic lava fields, snow-dusted mountains, and coastal fjords — a breathtaking introduction to Iceland's raw winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður mid-afternoon. Check in and settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord. Take a gentle self-guided stroll through the charming, snow-quiet streets of Siglufjörður — Iceland's northernmost town — visiting the iconic red harbour and the Herring Era Museum exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from the overnight flight. Enjoy a quiet, candlelit dinner at the hotel restaurant, sampling locally sourced Icelandic cuisine to ease into the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Keflavík Airport's premium lounge before departure from the terminal, or snacks provided in the private transfer vehicle.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box arranged by the transfer service, enjoyed en route with views of the Icelandic highlands.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes' in-house restaurant — Arctic char with dill butter, lamb soup, and skyr panna cotta. Pair with Icelandic craft beer or a curated wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer well in advance. The drive from Keflavík to Siglufjörður passes through Reykjavík — consider a brief fuel/coffee stop. January days are very short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30), so the drive will be mostly in darkness or twilight. Tunnel access through Héðinsfjörður tunnel is the final approach to Siglufjörður.

day_by_day.morning: After a restorative breakfast, visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore three authentic harbour buildings depicting the dramatic 20th-century herring boom that shaped Siglufjörður. Private guided tour available for a premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoe or winter hike on the lower slopes above the town with a local mountain guide. The surrounding Tröllaskagi peninsula offers stunning fjord panoramas and pristine snow-covered terrain. Alternatively, arrange a private snowmobile excursion on the mountain plateau above the town.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a guided evening excursion away from any residual town light pollution into the surrounding fjord valleys. Siglufjörður's remote northern location (66°N) makes it an exceptional aurora viewing site. Your guide will monitor aurora forecasts and drive to optimal vantage points.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and fresh coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kaffi Rauðka, Siglufjörður's beloved local café — hearty lamb soup and freshly baked bread.
meals.dinner: Return to Hotel Siglunes for a premium dinner — pan-seared reindeer loin with root vegetable purée and crowberry reduction.

day_by_day.notes: Aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions (KP index) and cloud cover. January in northern Iceland offers long dark nights (up to 18 hours), maximising aurora viewing windows. Dress in thermal layers — temperatures can drop to -10°C or below on clear nights. The hotel can assist with aurora alert apps and local guide bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula coastal road (Route 76) toward Hofsós — a stunning winter drive hugging dramatic fjord cliffs. Visit the Hofsós Infinity Pool, a geothermally heated outdoor swimming pool dramatically cantilevered over Skagafjörður fjord with panoramic mountain views. A truly world-class hot spring experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Skagafjörður region and visit Glaumbær Turf Farm Museum — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmstead offering a window into traditional Icelandic rural life. Then explore the small town of Sauðárkrókur before returning north to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy the hotel's premium amenities. If skies are clear, step outside for independent aurora watching directly from the harbour — the fjord's dark skies are ideal.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Hofsós or a packed premium picnic prepared by the hotel, enjoyed with fjord views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank with barley risotto and pickled red cabbage, followed by warm chocolate lava cake.

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is open year-round but check winter hours. The coastal road (Route 76) can be icy in January — drive carefully or arrange a local driver. Round trip from Siglufjörður to Hofsós and Sauðárkrókur is approximately 3–4 hours of driving total.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Akureyri region — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approximately 1 hour drive via the Ólafsfjörður and Dalvík tunnels). Morning visit to the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched dramatically above the city, followed by a stroll through the compact but charming town centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, serene and frost-covered in winter. Then explore the Akureyri Art Museum or the Nonni House museum. Alternatively, arrange a whale watching tour from Akureyri harbour — humpback whales are sometimes spotted in Eyjafjörður in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Akureyri at one of the city's finest restaurants before returning to Siglufjörður. Keep an eye on aurora forecasts for the drive back through the dark fjord tunnels and valleys.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rub23 in Akureyri — an acclaimed restaurant specialising in premium sushi and Icelandic seafood with an innovative menu.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — panoramic rooftop views over Eyjafjörður, with a menu featuring Icelandic beef tenderloin, langoustine bisque, and artisan desserts.

day_by_day.notes: The tunnel system connecting Siglufjörður to Akureyri (via Ólafsfjörður and Dalvík) makes this day trip very accessible — approximately 1 hour each way. Akureyri is a worthwhile urban contrast to the remote fjord setting. Book Rub23 and Strikið in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided ice fishing experience on one of the frozen lakes near Siglufjörður or in the Skagafjörður highlands. A uniquely Icelandic winter activity — drill through the ice and fish for Arctic char and trout in pristine glacial waters. Your guide provides all equipment and warm shelters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þórbergssetur) and explore the town's rich musical heritage. Alternatively, arrange a private photography tour of the fjord with a local professional photographer — the low-angle winter light creates extraordinary golden-hour conditions even at midday.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour (second attempt) — venture into the Héðinsfjörður valley or up the mountain road above town for an unobstructed 360-degree aurora viewing experience. Your guide will have scouted optimal locations based on the evening's forecast.

meals.lunch: Hot thermos soup and gourmet sandwiches provided by the hotel, enjoyed lakeside during the ice fishing experience.
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner arranged at Hotel Siglunes — a curated 4-course tasting menu featuring Icelandic langoustine, smoked puffin (seasonal), aged skyr cheesecake, and local spirits pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Ice fishing requires advance booking through the hotel concierge. January offers the best ice conditions. The private chef dinner should be arranged 48 hours in advance. This is a wonderful mid-trip splurge for a luxury experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður and begin the scenic drive south toward the Golden Circle region, stopping en route at Blönduós on the Húnafjörður fjord for a brief coastal walk and coffee. Continue south through the Icelandic interior highlands toward Reykjavík area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool (built 1891), a naturally heated geothermal pool at 38–40°C surrounded by bubbling hot springs, steaming geysers, and a dramatic winter landscape. Soak for 2–3 hours in this intimate, less-commercialised alternative to the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a premium Reykjavík hotel (upgrade from Siglufjörður base for the southern portion of the trip — recommend The Retreat at Blue Lagoon or Hotel Rangá). Enjoy a relaxed evening in Reykjavík's vibrant Laugavegur district.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Árnes Restaurant near Selfoss — traditional Icelandic lamb and vegetable stew in a cosy farmhouse setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a stunning New Nordic tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients and foraging traditions. Advance booking essential.

day_by_day.notes: Today involves significant driving (~5–6 hours total including stops). Depart Siglufjörður early. The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is a perfect mid-journey stop. Book Dill Restaurant weeks in advance — it is consistently one of the most sought-after reservations in Iceland. Confirm premium Reykjavík hotel accommodation before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle tour — begin with Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates visibly diverge. Walk the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley in winter silence, with frost-covered birch trees and frozen Þingvallavatn lake creating an ethereal landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes in dramatic plumes of boiling water against the winter sky. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January, with ice formations creating a spectacular natural sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Enjoy the city's premium dining scene and vibrant nightlife. Optional: visit the Perlan Museum for an immersive Icelandic nature exhibition and panoramic city views from the glass dome.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Hotel Geysir's restaurant near the Geysir area — fresh Icelandic fish soup and open-faced sandwiches with panoramic geothermal views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grillið Restaurant atop the Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — Reykjavík's premier rooftop fine dining with panoramic city and mountain views, featuring premium Icelandic beef and seafood.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is Iceland's most iconic day route. In January, roads can be icy — drive carefully or arrange a premium guided tour with a 4WD vehicle. Þingvellir is particularly magical in winter with minimal crowds. Dress in full winter gear for outdoor stops.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park — one of the world's most extraordinary dive sites. Don a dry suit and float between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility exceeding 100 metres. A truly once-in-a-lifetime experience. Guided by certified PADI instructors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Warm up and recover at a nearby geothermal facility. Visit the Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths on the shores of Laugarvatn lake — a premium spa with multiple steam rooms built directly over natural hot springs, plus a unique geothermal bread baking experience (rye bread baked underground in the hot spring).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Explore the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (exterior illuminated dramatically at night) and the Harpa Concert Hall. Attend a classical music or Icelandic folk concert at Harpa if available.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the Silfra dive (no eating 2 hours before diving).
meals.lunch: Late lunch at Laugarvatn Fontana's café — freshly baked geothermal rye bread with smoked salmon, butter, and Icelandic cheeses.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) in Reykjavík — an acclaimed seafood restaurant with Asian-Icelandic fusion cuisine, featuring sashimi of Arctic char, langoustine tempura, and miso-glazed cod.

day_by_day.notes: Silfra diving requires advance booking and a dry suit certification (or snorkelling option available without certification). Water temperature is 2–4°C year-round — dry suits are provided. The experience is physically demanding; ensure you are in good health. Minimum age 18 for diving, 12 for snorkelling.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — the crown jewel of Icelandic spa experiences. Book the premium Retreat Spa package for exclusive access to the private lagoon, in-water massage treatments, silica mud mask rituals, algae face masks, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lounge with panoramic lava field views. Arrive early for the most serene experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at the Blue Lagoon. Enjoy the in-water bar, the LAVA Restaurant for a premium lunch, and the various thermal pools and steam caves. The milky-blue 37–39°C waters rich in silica, algae, and minerals are deeply restorative after days of adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Enjoy a leisurely evening exploring the city's art galleries, design shops on Skólavörðustígur, and the vibrant bar scene on Laugavegur.

meals.lunch: Lunch at LAVA Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon — a stunning lava cave setting with floor-to-ceiling windows over the lagoon. Premium Icelandic seafood platter and champagne.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavík — a celebrated restaurant reimagining traditional Icelandic recipes with modern technique. Try the salt cod with brown butter, lamb head terrine, and skyr mousse.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance — it sells out months ahead, especially in peak aurora season. The Retreat package includes private lagoon access separate from the main public lagoon. Arrive at opening time for the most peaceful experience. Silica mud masks are complimentary and excellent for skin.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Reykjavík early for the South Coast. Drive the Ring Road east, stopping at the dramatic Seljalandsfoss waterfall — in January, the falls are partially frozen with spectacular ice formations. Walk behind the curtain of water (weather permitting) for a unique perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall — another iconic cascade, often with ice-encrusted rocks and rainbow mist in winter light. Then visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt columns, roaring Atlantic surf, and the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks rising from the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Hotel Rangá near Hella — one of Iceland's finest luxury hotels, renowned for its aurora viewing programme, private hot tubs, and exceptional restaurant. The hotel's dedicated aurora guide monitors conditions nightly.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógarfoss Café or a premium packed lunch from the hotel, enjoyed with waterfall views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Rangá's Aurora Restaurant — a celebrated fine dining experience featuring Icelandic lamb rack, lobster bisque, and a dessert trolley. The restaurant has panoramic south-facing windows ideal for aurora spotting during dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and stay well back from the waterline. The South Coast drive is approximately 3–4 hours from Reykjavík to Hotel Rangá. Hotel Rangá has private hot tubs on each cabin deck — perfect for aurora watching.

day_by_day.morning: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull — depart early for the Skaftafell area within Vatnajökull National Park (approximately 2 hours east of Hotel Rangá). Strap on crampons and harness with an expert glacier guide and hike across Europe's largest glacier. Explore stunning blue ice caves, crevasses, and glacial formations in an otherworldly landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most spectacular natural wonders. Watch enormous blue-tinged icebergs calve from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drift slowly toward the sea. Walk to Diamond Beach where translucent ice chunks wash ashore on black volcanic sand — extraordinary photographic opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Rangá. Soak in your private outdoor hot tub under the stars. Hotel Rangá's aurora guide will alert you if the northern lights appear — the hotel's south-facing location and dark skies make it one of Iceland's premier aurora viewing destinations.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Rangá before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch provided by Hotel Rangá, enjoyed at Jökulsárlón lagoon's edge.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Rangá — pan-seared Arctic char with fennel cream, followed by Icelandic cheese board and cloudberry sorbet.

day_by_day.notes: The glacier hike requires advance booking with a certified glacier guide — Icelandic Mountain Guides or Local Guide are recommended operators. Minimum fitness level required. The round trip to Skaftafell and Jökulsárlón is approximately 5–6 hours of driving — a long but spectacular day. Dress in full waterproof and thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at Hotel Rangá. Enjoy a late, indulgent breakfast and relax in the hotel's premium facilities. Optional: visit the nearby Hekla volcano viewpoint or the Þórsmörk highland valley (weather and road conditions permitting in January).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west toward the Reykjanes Peninsula. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the visible rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, a symbolic complement to the Silfra dive experience. Explore the dramatic volcanic landscape of the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunting Tour — book a premium private aurora tour from the Reykjavík area with a dedicated guide and photographer. This exclusive experience includes a private 4WD vehicle, professional aurora photography session, and hot chocolate under the dancing lights. A perfect final-night aurora experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at Hotel Rangá.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bryggjan Brugghús in Grindavík — a craft brewery and restaurant near the Blue Lagoon area, serving fresh fish and chips and locally brewed Icelandic ales.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Öxará Restaurant at The Retreat at Blue Lagoon — an ultra-premium dining experience in a stunning lava field setting, featuring a chef's tasting menu with wine pairing. One of Iceland's most exclusive dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private aurora photography tour well in advance — these exclusive experiences are limited and popular. The Reykjanes Peninsula has been volcanically active in recent years — check current conditions and any restricted areas before visiting. The Öxará dinner at The Retreat requires advance reservation and is a significant splurge worth every króna.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel. Last-minute shopping on Laugavegur for premium Icelandic souvenirs — Ístex lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, skyr products, and local design items. Visit the Kolaportið flea market if open (weekends only — check schedule).
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavík International Airport via private luxury car service. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Enjoy the airport's premium lounges before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry with you extraordinary memories of aurora-lit fjords, steaming geothermal pools, ancient glaciers, and the wild, elemental beauty of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast at the hotel — smoked salmon, skyr, rye bread, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Keflavík Airport premium lounge or a final meal at Reykjavík's Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic open-faced sandwiches and fermented shark (hákarl) for the adventurous.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Keflavík Airport is approximately 45 minutes from central Reykjavík. Duty-free Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Icelandic gin) make excellent final purchases. Ensure all aurora photographs are backed up before departure. January flights can be subject to weather delays — build buffer time into your transfer.
